brief.headline: A weekend de-escalation track has opened while the physical market stayed tight: the US paused strikes to give talks space and Iran-Oman deputy-FM talks in Tehran on Hormuz safe passage were called constructive, yet the last official (24-Jul) still shows a WIDENING cash-3M backwardation of +$14.50 and stock at a fresh 2022 low of 272,775 t - so Monday's ring reopens with a softer risk premium meeting a tighter curve.
bullets: What moved over the weekend: no LME session (Sat/Sun closed), so the benchmark is unchanged at the 24-Jul official - cash $3,175.00 (-$19.00, -0.59%) and 3M $3,160.50 (-$21.50, -0.68%), with Trading Economics' traded reference at $3,165.05 (-0.83%). Price remains ~$75 above the $3,085 four-month low: a give-back inside the rebound, not a break of it.

The new information is political, not price: the US allowed an apparent pause in strikes to let talks develop, and Iran's and Oman's deputy foreign ministers spent two days in Tehran exchanging views on shared principles and operational mechanisms for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz - described as constructive, with progress made. The American blockade on Iranian ports remains in effect, so this is a de-escalation signal, not a settlement.

The divergence still stands and matters more: on the 24-Jul official the cash-3M backwardation WIDENED to +$14.50 from +$12.00 while the stock draw ACCELERATED to -2,400 t (272,775 t, -46.4% YTD, lowest since 2022), with SHFE also drawing. The flat price is trading headlines; the spread and the warehouses are trading units - and prompt metal is still getting scarcer.

Watch this week: Monday's 27-Jul ring is the first price to see the weekend diplomacy - whether it prices the off-ramp (softer flat price) while the backwardation keeps widening, which would sharpen the squeeze signature rather than relieve it. Then whether the Hormuz safe-passage mechanism becomes concrete (bearish the war premium, and the route back for ~9% of global primary supply), and the pace of EGA Al Taweelah's alumina ramp as the main supply-side counterweight.

drivers.text: Shipping risk spans two waterways - and the risk premium is now clearly NARROWING — Hormuz remains strained and the Red Sea is a live front after Houthi attacks on two Saudi tankers, but the weekend shifted the skew lower: the US paused strikes to give talks space and Iranian and Omani deputy foreign ministers held two days of talks in Tehran on shared principles and operational mechanisms for safe passage through the Strait, reported as constructive with progress made. Brent had already settled $98.38 on 24-Jul (-2.29%) off the $100+ spike. Roughly 9% of global primary supply still sits behind these routes and the US blockade of Iranian ports remains in effect, so the floor is real - but a working safe-passage mechanism is now the most likely single source of premium compression.
drivers.source: CNN live updates - Trump admin signals pause in strikes will allow talks to progress; Iran-Oman Hormuz talks (26-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: US Section 232 at 50% - the tariff leg is ~66% of the US premium — Aluminium articles made entirely or almost entirely of aluminium pay 50% on full customs value (derivative aluminium content pays 25%); proclamation 01-Jun-2026, effective 08-Jun through 31-Dec-2027, CBP guidance CSMS #68855869. At the 24-Jul cash of $3,175 that is ~$1,587.50/t of pure policy cost inside a ~$2,420/t duty-paid premium, leaving ~$832.50/t of residual market premium. From 20-Jul a new incentive program lets approved companies investing in US primary capacity import tied metal at half the applicable rate.
drivers.source: White & Case - United States modifies steel, aluminum and copper Section 232 tariffs

drivers.text: Europe: war premium fading against a structural floor — Platts duty-unpaid P1020A in-warehouse Rotterdam sits at $525-560/t (mid $542.50, 03-Jul), down from $600-625 in mid-May as the Middle East war premium receded - a move that extends as Brent breaks below $100. The floor beneath it is structural: the 6% EU import duty, CBAM and idled European capacity, with Mozal still in care & maintenance.
drivers.source: S&P Global - European aluminum market seeks floor as Middle East war premium fades (07-Jul-2026)

drivers.text: Japan: Q3 settled at a decade high; the widening backwardation supports spot — Q3-2026 MJP settled at $395/t CIF Japan (Platts, 06-Jul), a decade high and the fourth consecutive rise ($86 to $195 to $351.5 to $395). CIF spot has eased to ~$365 with the risk premium, but the LME cash-3M backwardation widened to +$14.50 on the 24-Jul official - SMM's squeeze-risk flag on nearby units stays live into the ~September Q4 talks.
drivers.source: IndexBox / S&P Global Platts - Japan Q3-2026 aluminium premium hits a decade high at $395/t

prices.note: ~$68 CIF China (FOB Guinea ~$38, 45/3 grade); oversupply is deepening - Guinea shipped a RECORD 114.8 Mt in H1-2026, +15% y/y from 99.8 Mt, on robust Chinese demand (China took 82.57 Mt Jan-May, +24% y/y, ~82% of its imports); Metro Mining shipped a record 1.8 Mt in Q2 (+7% y/y). Guinea is reportedly weighing a 2026 export cap near 150 Mt (vs 178 Mt in 2025) to target >$100/dmt, but no formal decree has been issued and the record H1 flow cuts against it. (Mining Weekly, 23-Jul-2026)

notes: The alumina market remains the mirror image of metal: globally LOOSENING (EGA's 2.4 Mtpa restart at full output since 10-Jul, record Guinean bauxite exports, Chinese port stocks building; SMM Alumina Index easing toward ~Y2,700/t) - ex-China consolidation sits at ~$300-322 (FOB Australia ~$322, down from the $325-328 transacted early-July range).

The regional wrinkle persists but keeps easing: the shipping disruption still spans two waterways (a strained Hormuz plus Houthi attacks on Saudi tankers in the Red Sea), yet the war-risk cover embedded in the ~60% of Gulf alumina imports that transit Hormuz is re-pricing lower as Brent broke $100 on 24-Jul and a US-Iran diplomacy track was floated. SMM separately flags ex-China metallurgical-grade output down ~6% y/y in June.

The ore leg has gone the other way from the bull case: Guinea's H1-2026 exports hit a RECORD 114.8 Mt (+15% y/y), with China taking 82.57 Mt Jan-May (+24% y/y). Guinea's pending export-quota policy (a considered cap near 150 Mt for 2026, targeting >$100/dmt) remains undecreed, and the record H1 flow materially weakens the case for it biting in 2026.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: Hormuz traffic stays strained after a run of tanker interdictions and the US military says the waterway 'remains open with American support', but the direction of travel changed over the weekend: the US paused strikes to let diplomacy develop and Iran-Oman deputy-FM talks in Tehran on shared principles and operational mechanisms for safe passage were reported as constructive, with progress made. The US blockade of Iranian ports remains in effect. Roughly 80-85% of Gulf aluminium exports and ~60% of regional alumina imports use this route; ~9% of global primary supply sits behind the strait, so a working mechanism is the single largest potential supply release.

logistics.label: Red Sea corridor
logistics.note: Houthis struck two Saudi oil tankers (Encelia, Layla) in the Red Sea, and Asian buyers have begun rerouting Saudi crude via the Suez Canal and around Africa. The alternative-to-Hormuz corridor for Gulf exports is itself a war-risk zone - a second maritime chokepoint under active attack.

logistics.label: Gulf / Red Sea war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk quotes stay elevated with two fronts in play, but the premium is easing at the margin: Brent settled $98.38 on 24-Jul (-2.29%) off the $100+ spike, and the weekend brought a US pause in strikes plus constructive Iran-Oman talks on Hormuz safe passage. Retain elevated insurance, interdiction and deviation-risk assumptions in Gulf- and Red Sea-routed freight and delivered-cost models, but the skew on that cost line has turned lower for the first time in weeks.

logistics.label: Baltic Dry Index (BDI)
logistics.note: Dry-bulk freight (a separate, slower-moving cost line) eased to ~2,671 on 20-Jul, down 81 points and off a mid-month peak near 2,944 on softer Capesize demand. Price the two legs separately: dry-bulk freight vs. the Gulf/Red Sea war-risk surcharge (Trading Economics / Baltic Exchange).

logistics.label: Land-bridge / alt routes (Gulf, Kazakh oil)
logistics.note: The overland-to-Red-Sea contingency is less clean with the Red Sea under attack. Separately, the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended loadings at its Black Sea terminal after tanker attacks, disrupting ~80% of Kazakhstan's oil exports - a reminder that alternative routes are also under stress. Keep carrier capacity and lead times current for any Gulf-origin cargo.

logistics.label: Incoterms / demurrage
logistics.note: Attacks spanning two waterways keep force-majeure and deviation clauses live for any Gulf- or Red Sea-routed cargo; war-risk surcharge pass-through and interdiction/delay risk remain live contract points to negotiate cargo-by-cargo. Generic supply-chain observation, not company-specific.

row.label: Brent crude
row.note: SETTLED $98.38 on 24-Jul, -2.29% (previous $100.69), having traded intraday to ~$96.8 - a clear break of the $100+ spike after reports that Pakistan, with Chinese support, is seeking to revive US-Iran negotiations. Crude still ended the week up ~10-12% after the escalation. Offsetting: US Central Command ran a 13th consecutive night of strikes, Houthi attacks hit two Saudi tankers in the Red Sea, and the Caspian Pipeline Consortium suspended Black Sea loadings (~80% of Kazakh oil exports). Energy is the largest smelter cost line - the fading spike is modest cost relief for European and Asian smelters. (Trading Economics)

row.label: US Dollar Index
row.note: DXY 101.468, essentially unchanged and still firm after easing from a 15-month high. A steady-to-firm dollar is a mild headwind for dollar-priced metals; the risk-off bid faded with the oil pullback.

row.label: EUR/USD
row.note: EUR/USD 1.13667 (-0.09%). The LME-FX fixing was $1.13750 on 24-Jul vs $1.13950 on 23-Jul; ECB fixing $1.13770 (Westmetall). The oil pullback eases the near-term war-energy inflation impulse for the ECB, though TTF gas (~EUR 63/MWh, +1.9%) stays exposed to renewed Gulf/Red Sea escalation.

row.label: USD/CNY
row.note: Yuan 6.77162. China's Q2 GDP grew 4.3% y/y (below the 4.5% consensus); H1 unwrought-aluminium exports were a record 3.4 Mt (+16.3% y/y; June 711 kt), but the SHFE/LME arb has recovered and compressed the export margin - semis-export flow now faces reduction risk. China also imported 82.57 Mt of Guinean bauxite Jan-May (+24% y/y, ~82% of its total).

row.label: USD/JPY
row.note: Yen 163.780. A weak yen cushions Japan-bound cargo premia in local terms; MJP Q4 talks (~Sep) open against the decade-high $395/t Q3 anchor, but into a war-risk premium that is now narrowing rather than widening.

row.label: US 10Y yield
row.note: 10Y 4.687%, little changed as the oil-driven inflation impulse faded with the crude pullback. Real rates remain the macro cap on metals; this week's swing factor is the US-Iran diplomacy-versus-escalation balance.

headlines.title: Over the weekend the US paused strikes on Iran to give talks room, and Iranian and Omani deputy foreign ministers held two days of talks in Tehran on principles and operational mechanisms for safe passage of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz - reported as constructive with progress made. The US blockade of Iranian ports remains in effect. A credible Hormuz mechanism is the main downside trigger for the war-risk premium in both flat price and regional premiums.

The 24-Jul official widened the cash-3M backwardation to +$14.50 from +$12.00 while LME stock drew an accelerated 2,400 t to 272,775 t - a fresh low since 2022 and ~-46.4% YTD - with SHFE also falling. A falling flat price alongside a widening backwardation and faster draws points to headline-driven length exiting a market that is physically tightening.

Brent settled $98.38 on 24-Jul (-2.29%, intraday ~$96.8), breaking the $100+ spike after reports Pakistan, backed by China, is seeking to revive US-Iran negotiations - the first credible off-ramp headline in weeks. US Central Command still ran a 13th consecutive night of strikes and Trump weighed a 'massive' response, so the skew is two-sided rather than one-way.

Guinea's H1-2026 bauxite exports hit a record 114.8 Mt, up 15% y/y from 99.8 Mt, on robust Chinese demand; China imported 82.57 Mt of Guinean ore Jan-May (+24% y/y, ~82% of its total imports). Record seaborne length on the ore leg weakens the bullish read on the still-undecreed export-cap policy.

The SHFE/LME price ratio recovered, sharply narrowing the export margins that drove record H1 semis exports (June 711 kt; H1 +16.3% y/y). New orders are softening and semis-export flow faces reduction risk if margins stay compressed - a potential loosening of the export valve. Q2 GDP grew 4.3%, below the 4.5% consensus.

EGA's Al Taweelah refinery has been at full alumina output since 10-Jul, ramping toward 50% of capacity and full capability by end-2026; ex-China alumina eased to ~$322/t FOB Australia as the surplus deepens. The principal supply-side offset to the geopolitical risk keeps building.

US Section 232 stays at 50% on aluminium articles made entirely or almost entirely of aluminium (25% on derivative aluminium content), effective 08-Jun-2026 through 31-Dec-2027; from 20-Jul a new incentive program lets approved US-investing producers import primary at half-rate. At the 24-Jul cash of $3,175 the tariff leg is ~$1,587.50/t - still the largest administered component of US duty-paid metal.

Norsk Hydro's Q2 (22-Jul) beat with adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m (+14.5% y/y) on higher aluminium prices, product premiums and recycling margins, partly offset by reduced Qatalum output; Alcoa (16-Jul) posted record Aluminum-segment EBITDA of $1.073bn at a 32.3% margin on record $4.0bn revenue. The disruption-quarter price and premium are reaching producer margins.

forward.basis: LME official prices via Westmetall. Baseline = LME 3-month official (a traded market price). Range = random-walk cone from realized volatility. Driver score = 3 transparent rules, hit rate measured on history.
forward.source: London Metal Exchange official settlements via Westmetall (https://www.westmetall.com/en/markdaten.php?action=table&field=LME_Al_cash)
forward.stance_label: Current physical-market condition (diagnostic, not a forecast)

drivers.name: Curve carry (cash − 3M)
drivers.rule: Backwardation (cash above 3M) = prompt physical tightness = bullish; contango = bearish.

drivers.name: Inventory trend (13-week)
drivers.rule: LME stock falling more than 2% over 13 weeks = tightening = bullish; rising >2% = bearish.

drivers.name: Momentum (3M vs 20-week average)
drivers.rule: Price above its 20-week average = uptrend = bullish; below = bearish.

backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 39.6% directional hit rate against a 73.3% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 2.31% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (96 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-04-24). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

earnings.note: Q2 2026 BEAT: adjusted EBITDA NOK 8,923m (+14.5% y/y vs NOK 7,790m; above consensus); Aluminium Metal adjusted EBITDA NOK 6,421m; adjusted EPS NOK 2.2 (from NOK 1.7); free cash flow NOK 4bn; 12-month adjusted RoaCE 10.9%. Shares rose on the print. First European producer P&L of the Hormuz-disruption quarter. Higher aluminium prices and product premiums plus stronger recycling earnings drove the beat; a stronger NOK and lower hydro-power output were partial offsets. Confirms the disruption-quarter price/premium is translating into real producer margin - a positive read-across for the smelter complex.

June-quarter production report: Worsley alumina 943 kt, Hillside aluminium 179 kt; group beat FY26 production guidance with quarterly sales +15%. Sale of the aluminium value chain to Alcoa (announced 01-Jul) progressing. Upstream volumes intact and above guidance; the aluminium/alumina divestment to Alcoa repositions S32 as an upstream base-metals play. Confirms Western supply is expressing the Gulf disruption through price/freight, not lost tonnage.

Revenue $3.97bn (+24% q/q, highest in nearly a decade); adj. EPS $2.12 (MISS vs ~$2.31 consensus); adj. net income $562m; adj. EBITDA $901m (from $595m in Q1); Aluminum segment RECORD EBITDA $1.073bn at 32.3% margin. First producer P&L under the Hormuz-disruption regime: record aluminium margins and near-decade-high revenue on higher LME + strong US Midwest premiums, but adj. EPS missed on higher costs — notably ~$35m more Section-232 tariff on Canadian metal into the US — and the shares fell. South32 upstream acquisition ($4.1bn upfront, up to $5.6bn contingent to 2030) progressing, close expected H1-2027. The tariff is a double edge: it inflates US premia but taxes Alcoa's cross-border Canadian metal.

Q2 2026 production (14-Jul): aluminium 841 kt (flat y/y, +1% q/q); bauxite recovered from Q1 weather; alumina reduced q/q on Yarwun/Vaudreuil reliability events; group aluminium guidance intact 3.25-3.45 Mt. Kitimat, NZAS and AP60 continued their ramp-up while Arvida's final two potlines closed in June as planned, completing the transition to AP60. Steady low-carbon Canadian output into a tight, premium-rich market - constructive for realised margins even as the flat price eased.

Guides H1-26 net profit ¥1.8–1.95bn, +154.4–175.6% YoY. Credits industry-chain cost reduction, aluminium prices fluctuating at highs, high-value-added deep-processing mix and energy-saving retrofits — the first sizeable China H1 pre-announcement of the season and a positive read-across for Chinese producer margins.

Hindalco PAT ₹5,283cr (+66% YoY); India Al upstream EBITDA margin ~46%; Novelis FY26 adj. EBITDA $1.6bn (−9%). Record India operations; Novelis pressured by Oswego outage (~$104m) and tariffs (~$143m).

Net profit $200.3m (+316% YoY); EPS 53 fils; sales −17% on Gulf supply-chain disruption. LME averaged $3,195/t (+22% YoY) drove profit surge; volumes hit by regional conflict; ~19% capacity in controlled shutdown — restart path improves post-truce.
Adj. EPS $1.63 (beat $1.56); revenue $649m; net income $327m (incl. $288m Hawesville sale gain). Higher LME + strong US Midwest premiums; Q2 adj. EBITDA guided $315–335m.

Net profit SAR 1.63bn (~$436m, +5.5% YoY); revenue SAR 8.79bn (+3.2%); EBITDA $964m. Strong pricing across commodities; partly offset by lower phosphate volumes; 2026 capex set >$4bn. Ma'aden (1211) reports Q2 2026 on 06-Aug-2026; the Q1 print remains the latest public result.
Net profit guided RMB 5.30–5.59bn (+50–58% YoY). Strong on higher Al prices; China output near self-imposed 45 Mt capacity cap.
FY25 net loss $455m (vs $803m profit in 2024) on higher costs & lower output. Analysts expect stronger H1 2026 on higher prices; Asia pivot amid fractured trade flows.

caveats: Report refreshed Sun 26-Jul-2026 (weekend, evening London). The benchmark table and lme_series carry the latest PUBLISHED LME aluminium official - the 24-Jul (Friday) settlement, cash $3,175.00 / 3M $3,160.50 / stock 272,775 t, from Westmetall, re-verified against the source at this refresh. The LME was closed Saturday and Sunday; Monday 27-Jul is the next ring and officials print 13:20 London. This official therefore PRE-DATES the weekend diplomacy headlines described below entirely - no price in this report reflects them.

BOARD BASIS IS UNIFORM: aluminium, copper, nickel, zinc and lead are all set to their LME 24-Jul 3-month officials (Westmetall) - a single, consistent session across the board. Spot/CFD references (Trading Economics) are a different basis from officials and will not tie out exactly: the traded aluminium reference closed $3,165.05 on 24-Jul against the official 3M of $3,160.50, and Trading Economics' nickel ($17,310) and zinc ($3,589.65) differ from the LME officials shown.

YTD FIGURES ON THE BOARD are computed against each metal's first-published 2026 LME 3-month official (aluminium: $3,010.50 on 02-Jan-2026) and are indicative, not exchange-published index returns. Aluminium's -46.4% YTD stock change is measured from 509,250 t on 02-Jan-2026.

GEOPOLITICAL DEVELOPMENTS ARE FAST-MOVING and now materially post-date the settled 24-Jul official. Over the weekend the US paused strikes to let talks develop and Iran-Oman deputy-FM talks on Hormuz safe passage were reported as constructive with progress made, while the US blockade of Iranian ports stayed in force. Combined with Brent's break below $100 on 24-Jul, the near-term skew on the war-risk premium has turned from one-way escalation to two-sided and arguably lower. Treat the flat price as lagging the news flow, and note the internal divergence flagged throughout: price fell while the backwardation widened and draws accelerated.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY: MJP settles quarterly (Q3 $395/t, 06-Jul); Rotterdam duty-unpaid ($542.50, 03-Jul) and US Midwest (108.7-112 c/lb, 03-10 Jul) are assessed by Platts/Fastmarkets/SMM on their own schedules and no fresher public prints appeared over the weekend. The tariff/market decomposition IS refreshed daily because it is a function of the current LME cash. Figures shown are the latest PUBLIC prints, not daily marks.

ALL CONTENT IS PUBLIC MARKET INFORMATION for situational awareness only. No confidential, internal, company-specific or position data is included, and nothing here is trading, hedging or investment advice. Elliott Wave analysis is technical context, not a forecast or recommendation.

NO NEW EXCHANGE DATA WAS CREATED THIS WEEKEND. Every price, spread, stock and board figure in this refresh is unchanged from the 24-Jul official because no session took place; what has been refreshed is the narrative, risk-skew, premium-driver and outlook layer to incorporate weekend public news flow. The Elliott Wave counts are likewise unchanged - a count cannot advance without new price - and are explicitly carried forward, not re-labelled.
